baseline.what_exists: scripts/orchestrator_usage.py holds the resolution in one function: _cost_for(model, tokens, reported_cost, price_table) -> (cost, source) returning 'reported' when the provider gave a cost, 'estimated' from a price-table entry keyed by the observed model, else (None, 'unavailable'); _public_shape(cache, provider, price_table) builds the JSON the workbench and the usage command print, and it is where 'model' is read. The observed model comes from the event stream and is None for Codex by design (scripts/orchestrator_providers.py records observed_model = (None, None) and marks the dispatch audit_exception 'provider_default_used'). The dispatch's requested model is on the process record written by scripts/orchestrator.py as 'model_requested' (the same field the status listing prints); a record for movement NXS-LOCAL-0166 reads, in part: {"provider": "codex", "model_requested": "gpt-5.6-terra", "effort_requested": "medium"}. A usage row for that movement currently reads: {"provider": "codex", "model": null, "cost_source": "unavailable", "cost_usd": null, "input_tokens": 2973857, "cache_read_input_tokens": 2824704, "output_tokens": 23515, "total_tokens": 5822076}. config/model_prices.json already carries gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.3-codex and the Claude models, each with input_per_mtok, cache_write_per_mtok, cache_read_per_mtok, output_per_mtok. tests/test_orchestrator_usage.py holds the existing unit tests for this module -- follow their style.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every new branch names the clause it implements (GOV.ORCH.4-A CU-n).
Run only the two test files named in test_baseline plus the privacy gate.
Smallest diff; the resolution stays in one function, never re-derived at a call site.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.

risks: Collapsing the new source into the existing 'estimated', which would hide the uncertainty CU-2 keeps visible.
Reading the requested model inside the pure function by reaching for a file.
Changing Claude's output while touching the shared path.

in: Thread the requested model into the cost resolution: the usage functions gain an optional requested_model parameter (or read it from the process record where the public shape is built -- choose whichever keeps the pure function pure and say which in the SESSION_CLOSE), and _cost_for gains the CU-1 branch returning the new source string estimated_from_requested_model. CU-3: absent both models, unchanged unavailable. The reported and estimated branches keep their exact current behaviour.
The usage JSON keeps every field it has and adds nothing beyond what CU-1 needs; if the shape gains a field naming the model actually priced, name it plainly and document it in the module docstring.

The human-readable usage table (the 'cost' column of orchestrator.py usage) shows the estimate rather than a dash, with the source distinguishable -- a trailing marker is enough; do not widen the table's contract beyond that.
